strengths: The same chair, pedestal table and supported vessel set retain coherent scale, silhouette and material hierarchy in unrelated warm historical and cool contemporary rooms.

Rounded renderer-independent upholstery, physical piping, visible timber framing, brushed-brass accents and glazed-ceramic vessels remain readable at medium distance without external textures or renderer-owned bevels.
The vessel tray is exactly supported at the canonical 0.77 metre tabletop height in both seeded layouts, and the authored reading-corner recipe preserves its declared circulation corridor.

Layout-aware bounded adaptation of the verified warm-interior rig separates upholstery, timber, brass and ceramic while retaining zero clipped-white coverage and passing the tightened black-coverage limit in every semantic frame.
limitations: This release is accepted only for background and medium social-video framing; upholstery seams, joinery and vessel glaze are not hero-close inventory.
The chair, table and vessels are static geometry in this release; occupant seating, object pickup and dynamic upholstery behavior are semantic anchors rather than accepted animation.
The two rooms are verification hosts built to prove transfer, lighting response and circulation; they are not themselves publishable finished environments.
notes: V1 was rejected for inflated ellipsoidal cushions. V2 replaced them with tailored but visibly box-built upholstery. V3 exposed a camera outside the room shell and underlit modern materials despite passing permissive gates. V4 added live camera clearance, tightened black coverage and corrected exposure. V5 introduced a reusable renderer-independent rounded-box surface. V6 made lighting adaptation layout-aware. V7 fixes tabletop scaling so supported inventory is exactly grounded and is accepted only at medium/background distance.
